title: Ordinary coefficient square for a basic pair
statement: For fixed l,E,o,a, family X and integral inputs K, every BasicPair between expressions e and t has its ordinary reduction map followed by the system arrow equal to the reduction of the ringed arrow followed by the ordinary reduction of t.

source.place: Strict-system expression realization, generator square step.

proof.text: Case split on BasicPair. Apply ordinaryCanonicalIsoSquare to isoHom. For isoInv, precompose by reduction of the ringed forward isomorphism, use the forward square, and cancel the two isomorphisms.

For proper pullUnit and pullCounit, specialize the general mate unit and counit squares to the child ordinaryReduction and the inverse reductionPull isomorphism. For openUnit and openCounit, fixedOpenReduction_isIso supplies invertibility of the open mate at the child (or pulled-back child); specialize the inverse-mate unit and counit squares. Unfold only the ordinary coefficient recursion and the mate definitions.

Apply ordinaryProperOpenSquare, ordinaryExchangeSquare and ordinaryProjectionSquare to their respective constructors, with the actual maps and child expressions. Apply the two clauses of ordinaryCompactificationSquares to compactExchange and compactProjection.

proof_origin.place: C7: complete BasicPair case split, using the existing primitive squares and generic mate identities. Exchange is independently proved in the same delivery to remove its circular call to this theorem.

mathlib_searches.results: The source plan contains this generic intermediate as a private helper in IntegralBasicGeneratorSquare; it cannot be imported directly because that module depends on the assigned exchange module.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Split as a named intermediate theorem.
